text:
D2R Mobile

 An open-source compatibility layer for Diablo II: Resurrected with the Reign of the Warlock expansion, for iOS, macOS, Android and HarmonyOS. It brings the Nintendo Switch release you bought, expansion included, to iPhone, iPad and Mac in full: the original game code runs natively, every control is rebuilt for touch, the frame rate holds at 60 fps, and you are in a game one second after the main menu. There is now a native macOS version as well (first version): on an Apple silicon Mac it starts on double-click and works with keyboard, mouse and gamepad. Since v2.0 there is an Android version (community port): the same game program executes natively on ARM64 Android phones, with the graphics reimplemented on Vulkan; on a Snapdragon 8+ Gen 1 phone the camp and the Den of Evil and Cow Level fights all run at a median 60 fps (see "Android" below); a HarmonyOS version runs on the same engine (community port: an unsigned shell from the Releases page that you re-sign yourself, nothing to build; see "HarmonyOS"). Apple TV 4K (3rd generation, A15) has a community port (developer preview) that has reached the character-selection screen only on its author's device; see the device table below.

This is not a tech demo that "sort of runs". It is a mobile version polished for daily play, from your first character all the way through the endgame.

Platforms: iPhone / iPad (iOS 26 and later; iOS 18 – 25 with the older-API build) · Mac (Apple silicon, macOS 26 or later; macOS 15 – 25 with the older-API build) · Apple TV 4K (3rd generation, A15; community port, developer preview) · Android phones (ARM64, Android 12 or later, Vulkan 1.1; community port) · HarmonyOS phones (HarmonyOS NEXT; community port, unsigned shell from the Releases page that you re-sign yourself) · Game version: Switch release with Reign of the Warlock, 1.0.34.0 (corresponds to PC version 3.3.94012) · English / 中文 / Español / Русский / 한국어 · License: MIT · Bring your own game files 

中文: README.zh-CN.md · Español: README.es.md

 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 100% 60 fps about 1 s about 3.8 W 
 :---: :---: :---: :---: 
 The original gameplay, because it is the original program Steady, with no drops once the device warms up From the main menu into a game Whole-device power draw at 60 fps 

 What it is, and what it is not

 It is: 

- The game's own aarch64 program, executing directly on the device , with no emulated CPU. iPhone and Switch use the same class of processor; only the handful of instructions that cannot run unchanged under Apple's kernel are rewritten, and every other byte of the program is left exactly as shipped. Every class, every Runeword, Terror Zones, bosses, drop rules and quest flow are identical to the original.
- The platform services the game expects — system calls, the file system, the graphics API, audio, input — provided by a small host written for Apple platforms. The graphics API is reimplemented entirely — on Metal on Apple devices, on Vulkan on Android — with no emulation layer in between, and the shaders are translated offline from the game's originals.
- A port built for phones, and taken all the way: a complete touch control scheme, edge-to-edge iPhone and true full-screen iPad display, controller support, a power saver mode, save sync, six languages (English, Chinese, Spanish, Russian, Korean and Portuguese), and a whole set of endgame modes and quality-of-life features the original never had.

 It is not: 

- An emulator, cloud gaming, or streaming.
- A source of game content. It contains none and distributes none. There is no game program, art, text, data table or shader in this repository; all of that is generated on your own machine from your own files (see docs/GAME FILES.md). What the repository does carry is the interface information we recorded to make the port work — shader interface descriptions, the graphics API function table, addresses inside the program and the like — listed item by item in docs/DERIVED.md.
- Online. There is no multiplayer; the game runs fully offline and needs no online account.

 Battle-tested

All 44 iPhones and iPads in the closed beta — 35 devices registered for direct install (25 iPhones and 10 iPads), plus 9 TestFlight accounts with one device each — completed Normal, Nightmare and Hell with multiple characters , and the experience was excellent. From an iPhone 14 Pro Max with 6 GB of memory to the latest iPad Pro, not one device fell behind.

 Models 
 --- --- 
 iPhone 14 Pro Max, 15, 15 Pro, 15 Pro Max, 16 Plus, 16 Pro, 16 Pro Max, 17 Pro Max and more 
 iPad iPad Air, iPad mini, iPad Pro 11-inch and 12.9 / 13-inch (including M2 and M4) and more 
 Lowest model tested iPhone 14 Pro Max (A16, 6 GB): a flawless 60 fps 

iPhone and iPad share a single install package.

 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 Fast, smooth, and easy on the battery

Measured on a real device (iPhone 17 Pro Max):

 Item Reading 
 --- --- 
 In-game frame rate 60 fps , steady, with no drops once the device warms up 
 App launch 0.15 s 
 To the main menu about 1 s 
 From the main menu into a game about 1 s 
 Quick Restart, back in a game about 1.2 s 
 Longest frame when changing acts about 0.1 s 
 Whole-device power, 60 fps about 3.8 W (in camp, 50% brightness): nearly 5 hours of continuous play on a full charge 
 Whole-device power, power saver mode at 30 fps about 1.85 W , about half the 60 fps figure, for about twice the battery life 

 Measurement conditions: power is whole-device power measured on 2026-10-10 on an iPhone 17 Pro Max, standing in the Act I camp at 50% brightness, with 60 fps and power saver mode measured in the same scene; battery life is calculated from the measured power and the battery capacity, not by playing from full to empty. Launch and game-entry times were measured on the same model in 2026-10; frame rate and act-change readings were taken on the same model on 2026-10-12 while moving through areas and changing acts after entering a game. 

The install package is only a little over 100 MB.

install.title: Getting started
install.html:
Whatever device you play on, you start with the files of the game you bought: the Switch release of Diablo II: Resurrected plus the Reign of the Warlock expansion, updated to 1.0.34.0 (the version the console shows; it corresponds to PC version 3.3.94012, and the directory names and tools in this repository use the latter number). This project is built for the version with that expansion; using it without the expansion is not supported and has not been verified. How to prepare them is in docs/GAME_FILES.md.

This project provides only tools and an install shell that contains no game content. We do not distribute or endorse, and are not responsible for, any third party distributing game assets, game executables or install packages that contain game content. Please use only game files you legally own.

This project is implemented and verified on the Switch release 1.0.34.0 (which corresponds to PC version 3.3.94012), and by default the tools accept only that version. Community users have reported adapting other versions on their own by following the structure of this repository, and running them successfully. The rule tables are grouped by game version (in dm/tools/patch_nso.py, keyed by the build ID of the main program); you are welcome to contribute the version you adapted.

Check your device first and find your section in the table below; the "Which devices are supported" table above tells you which build to use on Apple devices and whether you also need a Legacy Device Pack.

Your device How Steps
iPhone / iPad, with an Apple silicon Mac (easiest) One-click packing and install with S2Arm "Easiest: one click with S2Arm" below
iPhone / iPad, with an Apple silicon Mac A full build from source "With a Mac: three steps" below
iPhone / iPad, without a Mac Download a shell with no game content and add your game content on Windows / Linux "Without a Mac" below and docs/NO_XCODE.md
Mac (Apple silicon) Build a native macOS App "Playing directly on a Mac" below and docs/MAC.md
Android phone Install the release page's APK and copy an import pack made on a computer to the phone "Android" below and docs/ANDROID.md
HarmonyOS phone Re-sign the unsigned shell from the Releases page with your own debug certificate, make a runtime pack on a computer and copy it to the phone "HarmonyOS" below and docs/HARMONYOS.md

The two routes for iPhone / iPad compared:

With a Mac Without a Mac
Computer An Apple silicon Mac with Xcode installed Windows / Linux / a Mac without Xcode
Method A full build from source Download a "shell" with no game content, use the packaging tool to add your own game content, then install it with a sideloading tool
Status The main route; everything above comes from it Works end to end on Windows, from making the package to playing on a device, and the game program produced on the two systems is byte-for-byte identical; the one step nobody has tried yet is signing with a sideloading tool — try it and tell us
Instructions The three steps below docs/NO_XCODE.md

The Apple account used for signing: a paid developer account gives you everything; a free Apple ID works too (no iCloud save sync, and the app has to be re-signed and reinstalled every 7 days). The full list of dependencies is in docs/DEPENDENCIES.md.

Easiest: one click with S2Arm (recommended)

S2Arm is our general Switch porting launcher, and D2R Mobile is the first "downstream deep port" registered in it: when you export this game in S2Arm, it asks whether to use the D2R Mobile route; once chosen, the packing underneath is this repository, and importing, packing, installing and pushing the game resources are all buttons in S2Arm — no terminal, no packing tools to install yourself.

  1. Install S2Arm on an Apple silicon Mac (s2arm.com) and let its environment check install whatever is missing; sign in to your Apple ID in Xcode (for signing).
  2. Add your game package (.xci / .nsp, with the 1.0.34.0 update) and prod.keys to S2Arm.
  3. On the Export page tick iPhone / iPad and click Export; when the confirmation page appears, choose "Use D2R-Mobile"; when it is done click "Install on iPhone". Your phone gets a separate D2R Mobile app, the game resources are pushed in by S2Arm, and it opens straight to the main menu.

Status: iPhone / iPad on iOS 26 and later works end to end (packed on a Mac, installed on an iPhone over Wi-Fi, in game); the older-API build for iOS 18 – 25 is not in S2Arm yet. Android, HarmonyOS, the native Mac version and S2Arm on Windows are not connected yet; use the sections below. S2Arm uses the D2RMobile-s2arm-bundle.zip attached to every release of this repository; the contract between the two is in docs/S2ARM.md.

With a Mac: three steps

  1. Put your game files in the workspace (default ~/dm-work, or set DM_ROOT):

    ~/dm-work/data/switch/3.3.94012/Update/ExeFS/    main, sdk, subsdk0
~/dm-work/data/switch/3.3.94012/Update/RomFS/    data/…

  2. Prepare the workspace. This checks your tools, rewrites the game program, and translates the game's shaders to Metal. The first run takes a while; later runs skip what is already done.

    ./setup.sh
source ~/dm-work/build/cache/dm/venv/bin/activate     # run everything after this inside the Python environment setup prepared; if you changed DM_ROOT, use it in place of ~/dm-work

  3. Fill in your signing details and build the app:

    cp dm/ios/local.env.example dm/ios/local.env     # set DM_TEAM_ID and DM_BUNDLE_ID; with a free Apple ID also set DM_FREE_ACCOUNT=1 and DM_IOS_UDID, and keep the phone connected while building
cd dm/ios && ./run.sh build    # targets both iPhone and iPad by default; for iPhone only: DM_DEVICE_FAMILY=1 ./run.sh build

The first time you open the app on your phone, it asks for the "game resource folder" — the 18 resource archives from your game files. Where to put them is in the section "The "game resource folder" that goes on the phone" of docs/GAME_FILES.md.

./setup.sh check is a health check: it reports the state of this computer, the tools, the game files and the signing configuration item by item, and for everything missing it says where to get it and which command to run next; it changes nothing. If what you have is a whole game package (.xci / .nsp), ./setup.sh <game package> <prod.keys> first extracts the game files into place and then carries on (install hactool first); if the base game and the update are separate packages, give both: ./setup.sh <base game> <update> <prod.keys>. Run ./setup.sh again after every update to a new commit: it rebuilds the patched binaries and the shader library for the current sources (steps that are already up to date are skipped). It also rewrites three files in the repository that change with your local tool fingerprints (dm/gfx/tools/dmsh_chain.lock, dm/gfx/nvn/dmsh_chain.h, dm/gfx/nvn/c1_full.tsv); that is expected, do not commit them.

Playing directly on a Mac

After the same ./setup.sh, one more command builds a native macOS App that starts on double-click and works with keyboard, mouse and gamepad, with no developer account:

source ~/dm-work/build/cache/dm/venv/bin/activate
dm/tools/mac_app.sh                  # macOS 26 or later: produces ~/dm-work/out/macapp/D2R Mobile.app
DM_MAC_M3=1 dm/tools/mac_app.sh      # macOS 15 – 25: produces D2R Mobile M3.app

The interface is the original's gamepad interface. Keyboard: Space confirms, Esc goes back, Return, the = key opens the menu / a new character, W A S D moves, and every other gamepad button has a key. Mouse: clicking a monster, NPC or object walks over and interacts, and the skill slots, potion cells and key hints at the bottom, buttons and tabs in panels, the class figures when creating a character and the minimap can all be clicked; clicking empty ground walks there and holding keeps walking, clicking a monster attacks it, and items take double clicks and drags. With a keyboard, the prompts on screen show keyboard keys. Saves stay on this Mac (iCloud sync needs a paid developer account and a build with DM_MAC_ICLOUD=1, see docs/MAC.md) and can be imported by hand from an iPhone / iPad. The key table, how to create a character, what the mouse can do, the import steps and the known shortcomings are in docs/MAC.md. Keyboard and a physical gamepad have not been operated by a person yet — if you try it, please tell us how it went.
